edges.note: The monotonic tag is exactly the Bass timestamp/sequence-number tactic: stamp state so an intervening modification (wrong ordering) is detected even when the value looks unchanged.
The tag exists only to make CAS loops safe; it widens the CAS-protected word with a version.
Single-writer ring-buffer pipelines (Disruptor) depend on release-store/acquire-load publication of sequence counters for cross-thread visibility without locks.
Balking is an interface-level state-validity check that rejects the operation instead of proceeding when the object is not in a sane state for it.
Same trigger (precondition not met): balking returns/fails immediately, guarded suspension waits until the guard holds.
PoEAA offline concurrency pattern: preserves isolation of a business transaction by locking an aggregate as one unit.

edges.cite: PoEAA, Coarse-Grained Lock: the shared version object variant is an optimistic offline lock over the group; a pessimistic variant is also given
edges.note: Fowler defines coarse-grained lock as either offline-lock flavor applied to a group.
The atomic read-modify-write primitive that lets many threads update shared state nonblockingly is what makes added parallelism (Bass introduce-concurrency) safe on hot shared data.
Condition synchronization is an arbitrator-connector service in the Taylor/Mehta connector taxonomy (concurrency control among components).
The CV wait-loop (wait while !guard) is the standard realization of guarded suspension.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.9 (Atomic Commit and 2PC): the coordinator drives participants through prepare and commit/abort phases
edges.note: The coordinator role IS the defining component of the 2PC architecture pattern.

edges.cite: Bass et al., SAiP transactions tactic: ACID transaction semantics most commonly implemented via two-phase commit
edges.note: The tactic names 2PC (whose engine is the coordinator) as its usual implementation.
Kernel- and task-level critical regions (scheduler/interrupt lockout) are the base mechanism protecting shared kernel and application data in preemptive RTOS designs.

edges.cite: Architecture of a Database System (Hellerstein, Stonebraker, Hamilton): the lock manager component includes a deadlock detector over the waits-for graph
edges.note: Named subcomponent of the canonical DBMS decomposition.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.7: under 2PL deadlocks occur and the database automatically detects them and aborts a victim transaction
edges.note: Detection is the standard companion to 2PL's blocking behavior.
Built-in per-task notification slots are the lightweight ISR-to-task and task-to-task signaling mechanism activating prioritized RTOS tasks.

edges.cite: FreeRTOS documentation (task notifications): positioned as a faster, lighter alternative to binary semaphores and event groups for one-to-one signaling
edges.note: Vendor docs state the substitution explicitly.
Removes repeated lock acquisition on the already-initialized fast path - per-event overhead reduction, Bass performance tactic.

edges.cite: Java Concurrency in Practice sec.16.2.4: DCL is broken without safe publication; making the reference volatile fixes it
edges.note: DCL is only correct when combined with a safe-publication idiom.
Kernel event-flag objects with AND/OR blocking are a standard RTOS primitive for activating tasks on combinations of conditions.
A synchronization object arbitrating when waiters may proceed relative to a monotonic count - arbitrator-connector service.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.8 (The leader and the lock / fencing tokens): monotonic tokens let resources reject writes from a deposed leader or expired lock holder
edges.note: Load-bearing safety mechanism for lock/lease-based leadership.
A concurrency-control mechanism: one combiner arbitrates and applies all pending operations on the shared structure.
Batching all pending operations under one lock acquisition cuts per-operation synchronization and cache-coherence overhead.
Kernel-assisted synchronization primitive; the substrate for user-space locks and condition waits.
Uncontended acquire/release stay in user space, eliminating syscall overhead on the common path.
Synchronous cross-thread invocation - a procedure-call connector whose access is arbitrated by a mutex.

edges.cite: Douglass, Real-Time Design Patterns: the Guarded Call pattern serializes callers with a mutual-exclusion semaphore
edges.note: The pattern's definition names the guarding semaphore.
State-dependent admission of callers is condition synchronization, an arbitrator-connector concurrency-control service.
Framework/layer-supertype code acquires offline locks automatically so the forget-to-lock fault class cannot arise (Bass exception-prevention).

edges.cite: PoEAA, Implicit Lock: framework code acquires whatever offline lock (pessimistic or optimistic) the scheme requires so application code cannot forget it
edges.note: Defined as a wrapper over the offline-lock patterns.
In foreground/background (superloop) systems, briefly masking interrupts is the mechanism protecting data shared between ISRs and the main loop.
The ISR-to-main-loop function queue itself must be guarded by interrupt masking for the architecture to work.
Critical region realized specifically by disabling/priority-masking interrupts.
One-shot gate arbitrating when waiting threads may proceed past a prerequisite point.
Standard lock-manager mechanism in the canonical DBMS decomposition, capping lock-table growth by trading granularity for footprint.
Escalation presupposes a granularity hierarchy with intention modes to escalate within.
Partitioning one lock into many raises achievable parallelism on a shared structure - the point of the Bass introduce-concurrency tactic.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.5 (Detecting Concurrent Writes): version vectors - vector logical clocks - are how Dynamo-style leaderless stores detect and preserve concurrent sibling writes
edges.note: Vector-clock variant is load-bearing for quorum replication correctness.
Causality tracking via logical clocks is what conflict detection/resolution between concurrently writing leaders rests on (DDIA ch.5 discusses version vectors for conflicts generally).
Scalable mutual-exclusion mechanism - arbitration with local spinning and FIFO handoff.
Queue-based spinlock variant eliminating cache-line contention of naive spinning.
The Disruptor ring buffer's lock-free producer/consumer handoff is built directly on memory barriers (per the LMAX/Disruptor technical write-ups Fowler's article references).
Explicit fences are the machine-level mechanism from which acquire/release publication ordering is built.

edges.cite: Mehta/Medvidovic/Phadke, Towards a Taxonomy of Software Connectors: arbitrator connectors provide concurrency control, with monitors among the named mechanisms
edges.note: Monitor is a canonical arbitrator-connector realization.

edges.cite: POSA2, Monitor Object: implementation uses monitor condition variables for state-dependent suspension inside the monitor lock
edges.note: Stated implementation structure.

edges.cite: POSA2, Monitor Object: uses the Scoped Locking C++ idiom to acquire/release the monitor lock on all paths
edges.note: Stated implementation structure.
Intention-mode hierarchical locking (Gray) is a defining lock-manager mechanism in the canonical DBMS architecture.
Provides the isolation half of ACID at mixed granularities for concurrent transactions.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.7: snapshot isolation for transactions is implemented with multi-version concurrency control
edges.note: MVCC is a named implementation technique of the transactions tactic's isolation guarantee.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.7: databases implement snapshot isolation using MVCC (keeping several committed versions of an object)
edges.note: Mechanism-to-policy relation stated directly.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.5 (Automatic Conflict Resolution): operational transformation is the conflict-resolution algorithm behind collaborative editors like Etherpad and Google Docs, framed as a multi-leader replication problem
edges.note: Kleppmann states the framing explicitly.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.7: serializable snapshot isolation is an optimistic concurrency control technique for serializable transactions
edges.note: OCC is a named route to transaction isolation.
Extends transaction-style isolation across business transactions spanning multiple system transactions (PoEAA offline concurrency).

edges.cite: PoEAA, Concurrency + Optimistic Offline Lock: presented as optimistic concurrency control applied at the business-transaction level via a version check at commit
edges.note: Fowler states the correspondence.
Global lock ordering makes circular wait impossible, preventing the deadlock fault class by construction (Bass exception-prevention).
Application-managed locks preserve isolation for business transactions that outlive any single database transaction.

edges.cite: PoEAA, offline concurrency discussion: choose pessimistic when conflict likelihood or cost is high, optimistic otherwise
edges.note: The trade-off between the pair is stated.
A resource-access scheduling policy bounding priority inversion and preventing deadlock under priority-based scheduling.
Makes schedulability analysis of preemptive prioritized task sets tractable by bounding blocking times.
The two standard real-time resource protocols; ceiling additionally prevents deadlock and chained blocking.
A scheduling-policy mechanism: temporarily boosts the lock holder so priority scheduling stays effective under contention.
Standard RTOS mutex feature preventing unbounded priority inversion in preemptively scheduled designs.
RCU keeps old versions live for in-flight readers while publishing new ones - multiple copies to eliminate read-side contention (Bass performance tactic).

edges.cite: Linux kernel Documentation/RCU/whatisRCU: presents RCU as a replacement for reader-writer locking
edges.note: The kernel documentation states the substitution as RCU's primary analogy.
Arbitrates access by operation class (many readers xor one writer).
Mutual-exclusion arbitration with owner/hold-count tracking permitting re-acquisition.
Multi-party synchronization point arbitrating when all participants may proceed; rendezvous is a classic arbitrator mechanism in connector taxonomies.
Handing objects between threads without corruption is the precondition for parallelizing event processing at all (JCiP's discipline behind the Bass tactic).
Managed-runtime services (GC, deoptimization, debugging) depend on safepoints to get a consistent view of every thread; a load-bearing VM mechanism.
RAII guard guarantees release on every exit path including exceptions, preventing the leaked-lock fault class; same move as Bass's smart-pointer example.

edges.cite: POSA2, Strategized Locking: parameterizes the lock type used by Scoped Locking guards
edges.note: The idioms are defined in terms of each other.
Converts one interaction policy (async signal delivery) into another (fd readiness) so a poll-based loop can consume it - the adaptor connector's mismatch-bridging role exactly.

edges.cite: Mehta/Medvidovic/Phadke, Towards a Taxonomy of Software Connectors: arbitrator connectors provide concurrency and access control via mechanisms such as semaphores
edges.note: Semaphore is the canonical arbitrator example.
Writer-priority arbitration where readers validate optimistically against the sequence counter.
Readers proceed without locks and retry on version change - OCC applied to a shared-memory read path.
All-or-none acquisition removes the hold-and-wait condition, preventing deadlock by construction.
Douglass's two deadlock-avoidance patterns attack different Coffman conditions (hold-and-wait vs circular wait).

edges.cite: DDIA ch.7: snapshot isolation is a widely used transaction isolation level (readers from a consistent snapshot, first-committer-wins writes)
edges.note: A named isolation policy of the transactions tactic.
Applies transaction semantics (atomic commit, abort/retry on conflict) to shared-memory state updates - the Bass transactions tactic in-process.
STM executes optimistically and validates at commit, aborting on conflict - OCC over memory words.
Busy-wait mutual-exclusion arbitration; the base mechanism for short kernel/embedded critical sections.
The synchronization mechanism becomes a late-bound parameter (template or polymorphic strategy), including a null lock - Bass defer-binding via parameterization.
Contention-reduced busy-wait arbitration reading from cache before attempting the atomic.
Spinlock variant that spins on a cached read.
Restricting mutable data to one thread removes interleaving nondeterminism for that data entirely (Bass testability tactic).
The single-threaded business logic processor is thread confinement applied at system scale: all business state owned by one thread, no locks.
Locking only at the public boundary and delegating to lock-free internals prevents the self-deadlock fault class by design (POSA2 motivation).
Recursive mutexes solve the same intra-component re-entry problem POSA2's thread-safe interface avoids structurally.
FIFO-fair busy-wait arbitration via take-a-ticket/now-serving counters.
Spinlock variant adding FIFO fairness.
Classical serializability protocol enforcing timestamp order on conflicting operations - an implementation of transaction isolation.
The textbook non-locking alternative to 2PL for serializable schedules.

edges.cite: DDIA ch.7: 2PL was for decades the standard algorithm implementing serializable transactions
edges.note: Named implementation of the transactions tactic's isolation guarantee.
The lock manager in the canonical DBMS decomposition exists chiefly to run 2PL.

notes: All 57 g5 elements bridged; none unbridged. Heavy reliance on arbitrator-connector for lock/synchronization primitives (semaphore, monitor, CV, spinlock family, latch, rendezvous, seqlock, futex, eventcount, RW-lock, reentrant lock, guarded suspension, flat combining): it is the ONLY arch element whose defining service is concurrency control, and Bass has no mutual-exclusion/resource-arbitration tactic. Missing arch targets that would improve specificity: (1) a 'resource arbitration / mutual exclusion' tactic or 'lock manager' DBMS-internal component (would absorb the DB locking cluster: 2PL, MGL, escalation, deadlock detection); (2) a managed-runtime/GC reference architecture (safepoint had only virtual-machine-architectural-style); (3) a collaborative-editing / real-time-sync reference architecture (operational-transformation routed via multi-leader-replication); (4) a distributed lock/lease service pattern (fencing-token routed via leader-election); (5) a reactor/event-demultiplexing arch element (self-pipe-trick routed via adaptor-connector). Sourcing leans on DDIA ch.5/7/8/9, POSA2, PoEAA offline-concurrency chapter, Mehta et al. connector taxonomy, JCiP, Douglass RT patterns, FreeRTOS docs, Linux kernel RCU docs.
